environment: dirty local working tree and loopback synthetic preview
applicability_reason: The planned public product models identifiable profiles, media, adult-age evidence, rights evidence and contact data for a Spain-targeted service.
expected: The production design should document controller/processor roles, purposes, lawful bases, transparency, minimisation, retention, recipients/transfers, rights, security and any Article 9 or DPIA decision before processing real data.
observed: The repository has strong fail-closed release, rights-evidence and contact/privacy gates, but the substantive privacy decisions and approved notices remain missing. The local preview uses fictitious identities and does not submit contact data.
method: Static review of release validation, contact state and legal intake; official GDPR and LOPDGDD source verification.
limitations: No production data map, provider contracts, retention schedule, record of processing, DPIA screening or rights procedure was available.
impact: Premature activation could process profile, media and contact data without demonstrable governance or complete transparency.
prevalence: Profiles, media lifecycle, contact flow and all approved legal content.
priority: P0 before real data or publication

source_refs.legal_effect: Directly applicable personal-data framework within material and territorial scope.
source_refs.version: EUR-Lex consolidated text, current version displayed 2016-05-04
source_refs.applicability_reason: Planned identifiable profiles, media and contact processing are personal-data processing targeted to Spain/EU users.
source_refs.verification_method: Official EUR-Lex consolidated text, legal status and scope/provision review.

source_refs.legal_effect: Spanish complement to GDPR within its scope.
source_refs.applicability_reason: Spanish-targeted personal-data processing and rights procedures.

false_positive_analysis: The current loopback preview has no real profiles and no enabled submission, so the observed gap concerns the planned production processing, not an assertion of active unlawful processing.
counterevidence: Release requires adult-age, consent, rights and content evidence.
Contact requires release, contact approval, privacy approval and exact destination match.
The synthetic preview visibly states that profiles are fictitious and contact is disabled.
remediation_minimum: Complete and approve the controller/provider inventory, purposes and bases, retention, rights procedure, privacy notices, processor/transfer terms, special-category analysis and Article 35 screening before any real profile/contact data enters production.
additional_hardening: Bind a privacy-design version and DPIA decision reference into the release snapshot and reopen approval when schema, provider or purpose changes.
suggested_owner: Controller, privacy lead and engineering owner
retest: Trace each real data field and destination against the approved record and test rights/contact flows in authorised staging.
residual_risk: High until substantive governance and production-provider evidence exist; low for the current fictitious local preview.
